def: The maximum number of tokens one model request can hold, covering instructions, history, documents and the answer being written.
Putting the whole corpus, or a large slice of it, into the prompt and letting the model find what it needs without an index.
Searching an index first and putting only the most relevant chunks into the prompt so the model answers from them.
The phase in which a model processes the whole prompt before producing its first output token, whose time grows with prompt length.
Keeping the processed prefix of a prompt for a few minutes so that a repeated prefix is read at a fraction of the normal input price.
A probe that hides one fact inside long unrelated text and asks the model to recall it, easy to pass and weak evidence of real long-context ability.
The decline in a model's ability to recall and use information as the number of tokens in its context grows.
The share of questions for which the context you built contained every fact needed to answer them.
A question whose answer needs a fact found in one document to locate a second fact in another, which single-shot retrieval often misses.
A hybrid that tries retrieval first and falls back to the long context only when the model judges the retrieved chunks insufficient.
Keeping lightweight references in context and loading the content with a search or read tool only when the agent asks for it.
